notes.meaning: Children naturally copy their parents, and believers are called to imitate God because they are His dearly loved children. God has shown great mercy and forgiven them, so they should reflect His character by being kind and forgiving to others. Living like God means letting His tender love guide how we treat everyone around us.

Believers are told to make love the daily pattern of their lives. Jesus set the greatest example of love by willingly giving up His life as a sacrifice on our behalf. In the Old Testament, a burnt sacrifice gave off a sweet aroma that pleased God, and Christ's death was completely pleasing to the Father.

God's holy people must turn away completely from sexual sin, impure habits, and greed. The word 'saints' means people set apart for God, so their actions should match their high calling. Sins that crave selfish pleasure should not even be treated as light or normal topics of conversation among Christians.

Foul language, foolish chatter, and dirty jokes have no place in a Christian's life. Such talk is useless and harms the soul, pulling believers away from God. Instead of using their speech for corrupt humor, Christians should use their voices to give thanks to God.

Paul gives a solemn warning that anyone who continues living in sexual sin or greed has no share in the kingdom of Christ and God. Greed is called idolatry because a greedy person puts money or possessions in the place that belongs only to God. Living in unrepentant sin cuts a person off from God's eternal blessings.

Believers are warned not to let anyone fool them with smooth, empty arguments that treat these sins as harmless or natural. Worldly teachers often try to excuse immorality by claiming God will overlook it. Because of such wicked actions, God's righteous anger is sure to fall upon those who disobey Him.

Christians must not join with unbelievers in their sinful practices. Sharing in their wicked deeds means sharing in their guilt and facing God's judgment alongside them. Believers are called to keep themselves pure and avoid partnerships that pull them into evil.

Paul reminds believers of what they used to be before coming to faith in Christ. They did not just live in spiritual darkness; their very lives were marked by ignorance and sin. Now that they are joined to the Lord, they have become light, so they must walk and act like children of light.

Living in God's light produces good fruit in a person's life. This fruit shows itself in kindness toward others, righteous living, and honesty in all things. These godly traits stand in total contrast to the hidden, harmful deeds of the world.

Christians must constantly examine their choices to see what truly pleases the Lord. Living in the light means learning by daily experience and prayer how to obey God's will. Believers do not follow worldly trends, but search for what honors their Master.

God's people must refuse to take any part in sinful actions, which produce nothing good and end only in spiritual ruin. It is not enough to simply stay away from evil deeds; Christians must also shine the light of truth on them. Exposing darkness means showing its shameful nature through a holy life and faithful words.

The evil deeds that ungodly people practice in secret are so filthy that it is shameful even to describe them. Talking openly about vile practices can pollute the mind and spread bad habits. Instead of describing every detail of wickedness, believers should simply show that it is wrong by living right.

When light shines into a dark room, it reveals everything that was hidden in the shadows. In the same way, the truth of the gospel exposes sinful deeds and shows how harmful they truly are. Once evil is brought into the open by God's light, its power to deceive is broken.

Paul quotes a call for sinners and sleeping believers to wake up from spiritual slumber and rise from the death of sin. Those who turn to the Lord receive life and spiritual light directly from Jesus Christ. The Lord dispels their darkness and gives them wisdom and hope.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars believe this passage quotes an early Christian baptismal hymn based on themes from the prophet Isaiah.

notes.meaning: Believers must look carefully at how they live each day, walking with great care and attention. Fools wander through life without thinking about where they are headed or what God requires. Wise Christians order their steps carefully according to God's commandments.

Christians are told to make the very best use of every opportunity they are given. The world around them is full of evil and distractions that can easily waste a person's life. Like a wise merchant buying up valuable goods, a believer rescues time from useless things to serve God.

Instead of acting thoughtlessly, believers are commanded to seek and understand what the Lord wants them to do. True wisdom is knowing God's revealed will in Scripture and obeying it in daily decisions. Christians should not drift through life without spiritual direction.

Getting drunk on wine leads to reckless behavior and a complete loss of self-control. Instead of being controlled by alcohol, Christians are commanded to let the Holy Spirit fill and govern their lives continually. Being filled with the Spirit brings true joy and self-control rather than shameful ruin.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the phrase can be translated 'filled by the Spirit', meaning that Christ uses the Holy Spirit as the means to fill believers with the fullness of God.

notes.meaning: A heart filled with the Holy Spirit overflows with joy and praise. Christians are to encourage each other by singing psalms, traditional hymns, and spiritual songs. True praise involves not just the singing voice, but sincere melody made deep within the heart to the Lord.

Believers should maintain a thankful heart, thanking God the Father at all times and for all things. Even during difficult trials, Christians trust that God is working for their good. All our prayers and thanksgivings are offered through Jesus Christ, who brings us into God's presence.

Christians are called to yield to one another and serve each other with humble hearts. This mutual yielding does not come from fear of people, but from deep reverence and love for Christ. Reverence for Jesus teaches believers to lay aside selfish pride and put others first.

differ.view: This verse sets a spirit of mutual humility that introduces God's order in the home, where specific roles of leadership and submission follow.
This verse gives a broad command of mutual submission that applies equally to husbands and wives, removing hierarchical authority in marriage.

notes.meaning: Christian wives are instructed to yield willingly to their own husbands out of obedience to the Lord. Their cooperation in the home is an act of spiritual devotion to Christ Himself. A wife honors the Lord when she respects the husband God has given her.

God has placed the husband as the head of the marriage, just as Christ is the head of the church. Christ's leadership is unique because He is also the Savior who gave His life to rescue His body. A husband's leadership is meant to reflect Christ's loving care, protection, and provision for his family.

Just as the church willingly follows Christ's guidance in all things, Christian wives are encouraged to support and follow their husbands. This guidance applies to all lawful family matters that align with God's word. A wife's submission is meant to be voluntary and guided by love, mirroring the church's devotion to Jesus.

Husbands are commanded to love their wives with the same selfless love that Christ showed for the church. Jesus proved His love by giving up His very life on the cross to save His people. A husband must never be harsh or selfish, but should sacrifice his own interests to care for his wife.

Christ died for the church in order to set her apart as holy and pure for God. He cleanses His people from the guilt and stain of sin through the power of His message. The spoken gospel brings God's forgiveness and works inward renewal in believers' hearts.

differ.view: The washing with water points to baptism as an outward sign and pledge of inward spiritual cleansing by the Holy Spirit.
The washing refers spiritually to the cleansing power of Christ's blood and the word of truth, rather than the physical act of water baptism.
The washing refers to baptism as an outward sign that conveys inward spiritual grace to the believer.
The washing refers directly to the water of baptism joined together with the spoken word of faith.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching understands this verse as a direct reference to the sacrament of baptism, which cleanses original and actual sin through water and the word.

notes.meaning: Christ purifies the church so that He can one day present her to Himself like a radiant, beautiful bride. When Jesus returns, the church will be entirely free from every moral blemish, spiritual stain, and weakness. Believers will stand before God completely holy, blameless, and clothed in His glory.

Husbands ought to care for their wives with the same natural love and attention they give to their own bodies. In marriage, God joins a husband and wife into one flesh, making them a single unit. When a man loves his wife, he is truly caring for an essential part of himself.

No one in their right mind hates their own physical body, but rather feeds it, clothes it, and keeps it safe. In the exact same way, a husband must tenderly provide for and protect his wife. Christ treats the church with this same constant warmth and nourishing care.

Believers are described as actual members of Christ's spiritual body. Because Christians share this deep spiritual union with Jesus, He loves and watches over them continually. Just as Eve was formed from Adam, the church has its life and being from Christ.

Quoting from Genesis, Paul recalls God's original plan where a man leaves his parents to be united with his wife. Marriage creates a new family unit where two separate people become one flesh. This physical and emotional bond is the closest and most sacred union on earth.

The bond between a husband and wife points to a much deeper spiritual truth that was once hidden. Paul explains that the earthly picture of marriage illustrates the profound union between Christ and His church. God designed marriage from the beginning to reflect this sacred relationship.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translated the word for mystery as sacrament, which Catholic tradition has cited as biblical support for marriage being a holy sacrament.

notes.meaning: Paul sums up his instruction for Christian marriages in practical terms. Every husband must love his wife with the same care he gives to himself, and every wife must treat her husband with genuine respect. When sacrificial love and willing respect work together, the home reflects the harmony of Christ and the church.
